question.worked_solution:
First, we write $2\,\frac{4}{7}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{4}{7}=\frac{(2\times 7)+4}{7}=\frac{18}{7}
$$

We also write $1\,\frac{1}{6}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{6}=\frac{(1\times 6)+1}{6}=\frac{7}{6}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{7}\times \frac{7}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18}{7}\times \frac{7}{6} & =\frac{18}{6}\times \frac{7}{7} \\  & =3\times 1 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
2\,\frac{4}{7}\times 1\,\frac{1}{6}=3.
$$
